question.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{9-(6x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{9(1-(6x-2)^{2}/9)}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{9}\cdot \sqrt{1-(6x-2)^{2}/9}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{3\sqrt{1-(6x-2)^{2}/9}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-(6x-2)^{2}/9}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-((6x-2)/3)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This resembles the basic integral for inverse sine:

$$
\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\,\text{d}u=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $(\frac{6x-2}{3}).$

So, let's perform the substitution 

$$
u=\frac{6x-2}{3}.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we write the integral in terms of $u,$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{9-(6x-2)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-((6x-2)/3)^{2}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{u}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{1}{2}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{6x-2}{3})+C\end{aligned}
$$
